detail.body:
**Issue**

`CPU_Accelerator.total_memory()` and `available_memory()` return host RAM from `psutil.virtual_memory()`. In a container or a Kubernetes pod, the process can use only its cgroup limit. Callers that plan memory from these values on the CPU accelerator include ZeRO 1/2 flattening (`stage_1_and_2.py:451`) and the autotuner. Fixes #8929.

Related: #1891 asks for cgroup-aware CPU memory limits. #3458 (Docker), #2632 and #2788 (Slurm) report processes killed by a cgroup limit without a message.

**Fix**

Only the CPU accelerator, its tests and its docs change.

- `total_memory()` returns the smallest memory limit from the process cgroup up to the root, capped at host RAM.
- `available_memory()` returns the smallest free headroom over every limited cgroup on that path. A parent limit also counts the usage of its other children, so each limited level is checked. Usage excludes the inactive page cache, which the kernel can reclaim.
- The cgroup mount point and mount root come from `/proc/self/mountinfo`. When several mounts match, the one whose root contains the process cgroup is used. This supports mounts that expose a subtree, cgroup v1 co-mounts such as `cpu,memory`, and delegated subtrees mounted before the main mount.
- On by default, as asked in review. `RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY_BY_DEFAULT = True` is the one line that sets the default. `DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0` turns it off, `=1` turns it on. `export_envs()` returns the variable, so the launcher forwards it to every node.
- The accelerator setup guide documents the variable. `abstract_accelerator.py` does not change.

**How to test**

Needs Docker with cgroup v2. Save the first script from the collapsed sections at the end as `check_cgroup_memory.sh`. One command installs `master` (before) and this branch (after) in the same container with 1 GiB. It prints `total_memory()` and `available_memory()` from three cgroups with `DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY` unset, and once more with `=0`.

```sh
sh check_cgroup_memory.sh "git+https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed@master" \
                          "git+https://github.com/prabhkodes/DeepSpeed@cpu-accelerator-cgroup-memory"
```

Output (Ubuntu 24.04 VM, kernel 6.8, 3.8 GiB, cgroup v2, Docker 29.1 with the systemd driver):

```
        process cgroup (container limit 1 GiB)                         total   available
before  A. container root                                          3904 MiB    2773 MiB
before  B. child cgroup, limit 256 MiB                             3904 MiB    2774 MiB
before  C. child 600 MiB; parent 800 MiB, sibling uses 500         3904 MiB    2685 MiB
after   A. container root                                          1024 MiB     342 MiB
after   B. child cgroup, limit 256 MiB                              256 MiB      90 MiB
after   C. child 600 MiB; parent 800 MiB, sibling uses 500          600 MiB     129 MiB
after   A. container root, DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0          3904 MiB    2755 MiB
```

Before, every case reports the host. After, `total` is the limit of each case. In C, `available` is the free headroom of the 800 MiB parent, which the 500 MiB sibling also uses. In A, the container's 1 GiB also holds that sibling. With `=0`, the values are host RAM again.

On a cgroup v1 host, the second script, `check_cgroup_v1.sh`, runs the same cases with the same arguments. Same VM booted with `systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=0`, Docker 29.1 with the cgroupfs driver and its default host cgroup namespace:

```
        process cgroup (container limit 1 GiB)                         total   available
before  A. container root                                          3904 MiB    2850 MiB
before  B. child cgroup, limit 256 MiB                             3904 MiB    2814 MiB
before  C. child 600 MiB; parent 800 MiB, sibling uses 500         3904 MiB    2781 MiB
after   A. container root                                          1024 MiB     175 MiB
after   B. child cgroup, limit 256 MiB                              256 MiB      89 MiB
after   C. child 600 MiB; parent 800 MiB, sibling uses 500          600 MiB     129 MiB
after   A. container root, DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0          3904 MiB    2672 MiB
```

Each script ran twice per cgroup version. `total` and the C row are identical in all runs. `available` in A and B reads live usage, so it moves between runs.

**Proof**

ZeRO training on the CPU accelerator, three Adam steps, flag `0` and `1`, two fresh containers each:

| processes | precision | ZeRO 1 | ZeRO 2 | ZeRO 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | fp32 | identical losses | identical losses | identical losses |
| 1 | bf16 | identical losses | identical losses | identical losses |
| 2 (`deepspeed` launcher, gloo) | fp32 | identical losses | identical losses | identical losses |

**Performance**

Throughput and peak RSS, flag `0` and `1` (`1` is the code path that is now the default), 30 timed steps on a 4×1024 MLP. Four runs per cell, two fresh containers, flag alternated. Median steps/s with range:

| processes | precision | ZeRO | steps/s, flag 0 | steps/s, flag 1 | peak RSS, flag 0 / 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | fp32 | 1 | 23.8 (22.9–24.7) | 24.2 (23.2–25.2) | 575 / 575 MiB |
| 1 | fp32 | 2 | 24.3 (24.0–24.9) | 23.3 (22.4–24.1) | 572 / 571 MiB |
| 1 | fp32 | 3 | 22.1 (21.1–26.5) | 22.1 (20.9–22.7) | 606 / 606 MiB |
| 1 | bf16 | 1 | 41.5 (37.7–42.4) | 41.2 (40.7–42.5) | 530 / 530 MiB |
| 1 | bf16 | 2 | 42.0 (40.1–42.5) | 41.6 (33.5–42.6) | 530 / 530 MiB |
| 1 | bf16 | 3 | 54.1 (45.2–55.4) | 54.2 (51.3–56.7) | 556 / 556 MiB |
| 2 | fp32 | 1 | 11.1 (10.8–11.4) | 11.4 (10.4–11.7) | 524 / 524 MiB |
| 2 | fp32 | 2 | 11.2 (10.3–12.4) | 11.9 (11.2–12.6) | 524 / 522 MiB |
| 2 | fp32 | 3 | 11.0 (10.7–11.1) | 10.6 (9.9–11.0) | 564 / 564 MiB |

Peak RSS does not change. The throughput differences go in both directions and stay inside the run-to-run range. A call counter shows why: ZeRO 1 and 2 call the memory queries once at setup, ZeRO 3 does not call them, and no configuration calls them during training steps.

Cost of one query, best of 5 × 5000 calls, process three levels below the cgroup root:

| | `total_memory()` | `available_memory()` |
|---|---|---|
| master | 12.4 µs | 12.5 µs |
| this PR, `=0` | 13.1 µs | 12.9 µs |
| this PR, default (on) | 81.5 µs | 80.7 µs |

Measured on ca6a5a6, before the default changed; the two rows are the same code paths. With the cap on, a query reads `/proc/self/cgroup`, `/proc/self/mountinfo` and the cgroup files: about 70 µs more, once per run.

```
pytest tests/unit/v1/accelerator/test_accelerator.py   # cgroup v1 and v2 host: 33 passed, 2 skipped
                                                       # in a 1 GiB container: 30 passed, 5 skipped (the pin_memory op cannot be built there)
yapf 0.43.0, flake8 5.0.4 --config=.flake8              # the pre-commit versions: no changes, no findings
```

Twelve new tests. They cover a limit on a parent cgroup, the smallest limit, the v1 sentinel, the headroom of every limited level, mountinfo resolution with several mounts, the launcher export, and default × override. One test uses `/proc/self/cgroup`, the cgroup mountinfo lines and the memory files captured in a Docker container on the cgroup v1 host above, so the v1 path is checked against a real layout. With the mount-root strip removed from the code, that test fails and the hand-written v1 tests still pass.

**Hardware.** Apple M4 host, Docker Desktop Linux 6.10 VM (aarch64, 10 CPUs, 7.8 GiB, cgroup v2). Python 3.12.16, torch 2.14.1+cpu, `DS_BUILD_OPS=0`. No GPU. cgroup v1, the v2 re-run and the unit tests above: Lima VM on the same host, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-142 (aarch64, 4 vCPU, 3.8 GiB), Docker 29.1.3, Python 3.12.16, torch 2.15.0+cpu.

**Compatibility matrix.**
- Validated: CPU accelerator; ZeRO 1, 2 and 3; fp32 and bf16; 1 and 2 processes; no offload. Memory values on cgroup v1 and v2.
- Not reachable on the CPU accelerator: `deepspeed.compile` (`is_deepcompile_supported()` requires CUDA) and the inference v2 KV cache (CUDA kernels only).
- Not validated: CPU and NVMe offload, fp16, multi-node runs (the launcher export is unit-tested only).
- Not affected: CUDA, XPU, NPU, MLU, HPU, SDAA, SUPA and MPS read their own device memory. `see_memory_usage()` and the timer read host RAM only to log it.

No open PR changes the CPU accelerator memory functions (searched `cgroup`, `cpu_accelerator available_memory`, `cpu accelerator memory`, `1891 in:body` on 2026-10-27).
AI assistance was used: an AI coding agent (Claude Code) wrote the change and the tests; I reviewed each changed line and ran the tests, the reproduction and the ZeRO runs.

<summary>check_cgroup_memory.sh (cgroup v2)</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Before/after check of DeepSpeed's CPU accelerator memory values inside cgroups. Needs Docker with cgroup v2.
#   sh check_cgroup_memory.sh <before pip spec> <after pip spec>
# Example:
#   sh check_cgroup_memory.sh "git+https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed@master" \
#                             "git+https://github.com/prabhkodes/DeepSpeed@cpu-accelerator-cgroup-memory"
# A pip spec can also be a source tarball in the directory given as SRC_DIR (mounted at /src).
# IMG replaces the python:3.12-slim image, e.g. with one that has torch installed.
set -eu
docker run --rm -i --privileged --cgroupns=private --memory=1g ${EXTRA_DOCKER_ARGS:-} ${SRC_DIR:+-v "$SRC_DIR:/src:ro"} \
  -e BEFORE="${1:?before spec}" -e AFTER="${2:?after spec}" "${IMG:-python:3.12-slim}" sh -s <<'INNER'
set -e
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
apt-get -qq update >/dev/null 2>&1 && apt-get -qq install -y git >/dev/null 2>&1
pip install -q torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu >/dev/null 2>&1
pip install -q psutil numpy pydantic packaging py-cpuinfo tqdm hjson msgpack ninja einops >/dev/null 2>&1
cat > /tmp/probe.py <<'PY'
from deepspeed.accelerator import get_accelerator
a = get_accelerator()
print(f"{a.total_memory() >> 20:>7} MiB {a.available_memory() >> 20:>7} MiB")
PY
cat > /tmp/hold.py <<'PY'
import time
b = b"\x01" * (500 << 20)
time.sleep(3600)
PY
C=/sys/fs/cgroup
mkdir -p $C/init; for p in $(cat $C/cgroup.procs); do echo $p > $C/init/cgroup.procs 2>/dev/null || true; done
echo "+memory" > $C/cgroup.subtree_control
mkdir -p $C/nested; echo $((256 << 20)) > $C/nested/memory.max
mkdir -p $C/shared; echo $((800 << 20)) > $C/shared/memory.max; echo 0 > $C/shared/memory.swap.max
echo "+memory" > $C/shared/cgroup.subtree_control
mkdir -p $C/shared/sibling $C/shared/me; echo $((600 << 20)) > $C/shared/me/memory.max
sh -c "echo \$\$ > $C/shared/sibling/cgroup.procs; echo -1000 > /proc/self/oom_score_adj; exec python /tmp/hold.py" &
sleep 3
# run <version> <label> <cgroup> [VAR=value]: the probe runs with the flag unset unless given.
run() {
  printf "%-7s %-56s" "$1" "$2"
  sh -c "echo \$\$ > $C/$3/cgroup.procs; DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu ${4:-} exec python /tmp/probe.py 2>/dev/null"
}
printf "%-7s %-56s %11s %11s\n" "" "process cgroup (container limit 1 GiB)" "total" "available"
for v in before after; do
  if [ $v = before ]; then spec=$BEFORE; else spec=$AFTER; fi
  DS_BUILD_OPS=0 pip install -q --no-deps --force-reinstall "$spec" >/dev/null 2>&1
  run $v "A. container root" init
  run $v "B. child cgroup, limit 256 MiB" nested
  run $v "C. child 600 MiB; parent 800 MiB, sibling uses 500" shared/me
done
run after "A. container root, DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0" init DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0
INNER
```

echo $((600 << 20)) > $C/shared/me/memory.limit_in_bytes

  run $v "B. child cgroup, limit 256 MiB" nested
  run $v "C. child 600 MiB; parent 800 MiB, sibling uses 500" shared/me

run after "A. container root, DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0" . DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0
# The files the CPU accelerator reads, as seen from cgroup C.
sh -c "echo \$\$ > $C/shared/me/cgroup.procs
  echo '### /proc/self/cgroup'; cat /proc/self/cgroup
  echo '### /proc/self/mountinfo (cgroup lines)'; grep -E ' - cgroup2? ' /proc/self/mountinfo
  for d in $C/shared/me $C/shared $C; do
    echo \"### \$d\"
    for f in memory.limit_in_bytes memory.usage_in_bytes; do echo \"\$f \$(cat \$d/\$f)\"; done
    grep -E '^total_inactive_file ' \$d/memory.stat
  done
  echo '### /sys/fs/cgroup/unified'; ls /sys/fs/cgroup/unified | tr '\n' ' '; echo"
INNER

**Precedent.** The same walk is already in production elsewhere. Rust's `std::thread::available_parallelism` takes the smallest `cpu.max` from the process cgroup up to the mount ([`quota_v2`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/41089d07a0a2afc16adfe28a760d94d73d7298a4/library/std/src/sys/thread/unix.rs#L908-L953)). The JDK fixed limits on parent nested cgroups in [JDK-8322420](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8322420) (2024) and the hierarchical memory limit in [JDK-8370572](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8370572) (2025). Go 1.25 finds the process cgroup through `/proc/self/cgroup` and `/proc/self/mountinfo` ([`cgroup_linux.go`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/63313a0fc5b68d86399a64e323113667d8aa7823/src/runtime/cgroup_linux.go#L11-L24)), reading the leaf only. vLLM's CPU-quota reader walks the hierarchy ([`_cgroup_cpu_limit`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ed6b8f4cd2b47e4240e7ff5feb5105444245b0c2/vllm/utils/torch_utils.py#L180-L231)); vllm-project/vllm#64104 adds the same for memory. The same fix for OpenObserve merged on 2026-10-28 (openobserve/openobserve#15906).

     oneccl_imported_p = False
 
 import os
+import sys
+
+# Default for capping total_memory() and available_memory() at the cgroup memory limit of the process. On, because
+# the kernel enforces that limit, so host RAM overstates what the process can use; DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=0 or
+# =1 overrides it.
+RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY_BY_DEFAULT = True
+
+_CGROUP_ROOT = "/sys/fs/cgroup"
+_PROC_SELF_CGROUP = "/proc/self/cgroup"
+_PROC_SELF_MOUNTINFO = "/proc/self/mountinfo"
+# cgroup v1 reports "no limit" as a huge sentinel instead of "max".
+_CGROUP_UNLIMITED = 1 << 62
+
+
+def _read_cgroup_int(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            value = f.read().strip()
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    return int(value) if value.isdigit() else None
+
+
+def _read_memory_stat(path, key):
+    try:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            for line in f:
+                name, _, value = line.partition(" ")
+                if name == key:
+                    return int(value)
+    except (OSError, ValueError):
+        pass
+    return 0
+
+
+def _path_parts(path):
+    return [part for part in path.split("/") if part]
+
+
+def _cgroup_membership(controller):
+    """The cgroup path of this process from /proc/self/cgroup, relative to the hierarchy root."""
+    try:
+        with open(_PROC_SELF_CGROUP) as f:
+            for line in f:
+                parts = line.strip().split(":", 2)
+                if len(parts) != 3:
+                    continue
+                is_v2 = controller is None and parts[0] == "0" and parts[1] == ""
+                is_v1 = controller is not None and controller in parts[1].split(",")
+                if is_v2 or is_v1:
+                    return parts[2]
+    except OSError:
+        pass
+    return ""
+
+
+def _cgroup_mount(controller, membership):
+    """Returns (mount point, mount root) of the cgroup hierarchy from /proc/self/mountinfo.
+
+    The mount can expose a subtree of the hierarchy (mount root other than "/"), cgroup v1 can co-mount controllers
+    under a name such as "cpu,memory", and several mounts can match, e.g. a delegated subtree mounted before the main
+    one. The mount whose root contains the membership is used; among those, the shortest root, because it
+    exposes the most ancestors and an ancestor limit still applies.
+    """
+    candidates = []
+    try:
+        with open(_PROC_SELF_MOUNTINFO) as f:
+            for line in f:
+                before, separator, after = line.partition(" - ")
+                mount_fields = before.split()
+                fs_fields = after.split()
+                if not separator or len(mount_fields) < 5 or len(fs_fields) < 3:
+                    continue
+                fs_type = fs_fields[0]
+                super_options = fs_fields[2].split(",")
+                is_v2 = controller is None and fs_type == "cgroup2"
+                is_v1 = controller is not None and fs_type == "cgroup" and controller in super_options
+                if is_v2 or is_v1:
+                    # mountinfo escapes spaces as \040.
+                    candidates.append((mount_fields[4].replace("\\040", " "), mount_fields[3].replace("\\040", " ")))
+    except OSError:
+        pass
+    member_parts = _path_parts(membership)
+    containing = [(mount_point, mount_root) for mount_point, mount_root in candidates
+                  if member_parts[:len(_path_parts(mount_root))] == _path_parts(mount_root)]
+    if containing:
+        return min(containing, key=lambda mount: len(_path_parts(mount[1])))
+    if candidates:
+        return candidates[0]
+    default_mount = _CGROUP_ROOT if controller is None else os.path.join(_CGROUP_ROOT, controller)
+    return default_mount, "/"
+
+
+def _cgroup_dirs(controller):
+    """Directories of this process's cgroup, nearest first, mount point last."""
+    membership = _cgroup_membership(controller)
+    mount_point, mount_root = _cgroup_mount(controller, membership)
+    components = _path_parts(membership)
+    root_components = _path_parts(mount_root)
+    if ".." in components:
+        # A cgroup outside this cgroup namespace cannot be resolved from here.
+        components = []
+    elif components[:len(root_components)] == root_components:
+        # /proc/self/cgroup is relative to the hierarchy root; the mount starts at mount_root.
+        components = components[len(root_components):]
+    dirs = [os.path.join(mount_point, *components[:depth]) for depth in range(len(components), 0, -1)]
+    return dirs + [mount_point]
+
+
+def _cgroup_memory():
+    """Returns (limit, available) in bytes for the cgroups that limit this process, or None.
+
+    The limit is the smallest one from the process's cgroup up to the root. Available memory is the smallest headroom
+    over every limited level, because a parent's limit also counts the usage of its other children. Usage excludes the
+    inactive page cache, which the kernel can reclaim. Available is None when no limited level exposes its usage.
+    """
+    override = os.environ.get("DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY")
+    enabled = RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY_BY_DEFAULT if override is None else override.strip().lower() in ("1", "true")
+    if not enabled or not sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
+        return None
+    for controller, limit_file, usage_file, inactive_key in (
+        (None, "memory.max", "memory.current", "inactive_file"),
+        ("memory", "memory.limit_in_bytes", "memory.usage_in_bytes", "total_inactive_file"),
+    ):
+        limit = None
+        available = None
+        for cgroup_dir in _cgroup_dirs(controller):
+            level_limit = _read_cgroup_int(os.path.join(cgroup_dir, limit_file))
+            if level_limit is None or level_limit >= _CGROUP_UNLIMITED:
+                continue
+            limit = level_limit if limit is None else min(limit, level_limit)
+            usage = _read_cgroup_int(os.path.join(cgroup_dir, usage_file))
+            if usage is None:
+                continue
+            inactive_file = _read_memory_stat(os.path.join(cgroup_dir, "memory.stat"), inactive_key)
+            headroom = max(0, level_limit - max(0, usage - inactive_file))
+            available = headroom if available is None else min(available, headroom)
+        if limit is not None:
+            return limit, available
+    return None

When the process cgroup has the smallest (or tied) `memory.max` but a larger-limit ancestor is nearly full because sibling cgroups consume it, this selects the child and reads only the child's usage. cgroup=0::/  memory.max=1073741824

BEFORE (stock 0.19.8):
  total_mib 7934   available_mib 5102        # host RAM

AFTER (this PR, DS_CPU_RESPECT_CGROUP_MEMORY=1):
  total_mib 1024   available_mib 838

AFTER (this PR, flag unset):
  total_mib 7934   available_mib 4963
```

So the cap works on a real v2 hierarchy, `available_memory()` is bounded by the cgroup headroom rather than host-wide `psutil` availability, and the opt-out path is unchanged. The PR's own test file also passes here: `32 passed, 2 skipped`.
